bss.topic: Coordenadas geográficas e fusos horários do Brasil

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual linha imaginária divide a Terra em hemisfério Norte e hemisfério Sul?
questions.hint: Ela é a maior das paralelas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual linha imaginária é a referência (0°) para medir a longitude?
questions.hint: É um meridiano, que vai de polo a polo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A latitude mede a distância de um ponto até…
questions.hint: Ela vai de 0° a 90° para norte ou sul.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o valor máximo da latitude, em graus?
questions.hint: É o valor nos polos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o valor máximo da longitude, em graus, para leste ou oeste?
questions.hint: Metade de uma volta completa de 360°.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em relação ao Meridiano de Greenwich, todo o território brasileiro fica no hemisfério…
questions.hint: O Brasil fica nas Américas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual trópico atravessa o estado de São Paulo?
questions.hint: É o trópico do hemisfério Sul.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas capitais brasileiras é cortada pela Linha do Equador?
questions.hint: Fica no estado do Amapá, bem ao norte.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Cada fuso horário corresponde a quantos graus de longitude?
questions.hint: Divida 360° pelas 24 horas do dia.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quantos fusos horários o Brasil tem atualmente?
questions.hint: Conte: ilhas oceânicas, Brasília, parte do Norte/Centro-Oeste e Acre.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o fuso horário oficial de Brasília em relação a Greenwich (UTC)?
questions.hint: São Paulo usa o mesmo horário de Brasília.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual estado brasileiro está no fuso UTC-5?
questions.hint: É o fuso mais a oeste do país.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quando são 12h em Brasília, que horas são no Acre (UTC-5)? Responda só o número da hora.
questions.hint: O Acre está 2 horas atrás de Brasília.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que os lugares mais a leste veem o Sol nascer antes?
options: Porque a Terra gira de oeste para leste
Porque o Sol gira ao redor do Brasil
Porque estão mais perto do Equador
questions.answer: Porque a Terra gira de oeste para leste
questions.hint: Pense no movimento de rotação.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quando são 15h em Brasília (UTC-3), que horas são em Fernando de Noronha (UTC-2)? Responda só o número da hora.
questions.hint: Noronha fica mais a leste: está à frente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que um país grande no sentido leste-oeste, como o Brasil, precisa de mais de um fuso horário.
questions.hint: Pense na rotação da Terra e na hora em que o Sol nasce em cada lugar.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is a storyboard used for when designing a game?
options: Sketching the main screens and events in order
questions.answer: Sketching the main screens and events in order
questions.hint: Think of a comic strip for your game.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does decomposition mean?
options: Breaking a big problem into smaller tasks
questions.answer: Breaking a big problem into smaller tasks
questions.hint: Smaller pieces are easier to solve.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Scratch, what is a sprite?
options: A character or object that can be programmed
questions.answer: A character or object that can be programmed
questions.hint: The cat is the default one.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Scratch, what is the background image of the stage called?
questions.hint: It is not a costume; it belongs to the stage.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which is a requirement for a game?
options: The player must be able to move the sprite with arrow keys
Scratch was made in a university
questions.answer: The player must be able to move the sprite with arrow keys
questions.hint: A requirement says what the game must do.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which task is the best example of decomposing a 'catch the falling apples' game?
options: Make apples fall from random positions
questions.answer: Make apples fall from random positions
questions.hint: A good task is small and specific.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why should you plan a game before you start coding?
options: So you never need to test it
To know what to build and avoid wasting time
Because Scratch will not open otherwise
questions.answer: To know what to build and avoid wasting time
questions.hint: Think about building a house without a plan.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which Scratch event block is commonly used to start a game?
questions.hint: It is in the Events category and has a coloured symbol.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What should a game's 'success criteria' describe?
options: How you will know the game works as planned
questions.answer: How you will know the game works as planned
questions.hint: They help you check and test.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A game needs a score that goes up by 1 each time an apple is caught. What do you need to create?
questions.hint: It stores a value that can change.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these belongs on a storyboard frame?
options: A sketch of the start screen with notes on what happens
The full list of every block
questions.answer: A sketch of the start screen with notes on what happens
questions.hint: Storyboards show scenes, not code.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which order makes the most sense for a game project?
questions.hint: Design comes first.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the 'target audience' of a game?
options: The people the game is made for
questions.answer: The people the game is made for
questions.hint: Who will play it?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Ravi's game idea is 'a space game'. Which question would best help him decompose it?
options: What should the player control and what is the goal?
questions.answer: What should the player control and what is the goal?
questions.hint: Focus on what the game needs to do.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: List three smaller tasks you would split a simple maze game into.
questions.hint: Think about the player, the walls and how you win.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why do you think it helps to share your storyboard with a friend before coding?
questions.hint: Think about feedback and spotting problems early.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does 'pace' mean in storytelling?
options: How fast or slow you speak
How long the story is written
questions.answer: How fast or slow you speak
questions.hint: Think about speed.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is intonation?
options: The rise and fall of your voice
The number of words in a story
questions.answer: The rise and fall of your voice
questions.hint: It is about the music of your voice.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why is eye contact important when telling a story?
options: It keeps the audience engaged and connected
questions.answer: It keeps the audience engaged and connected
questions.hint: Think about how the listeners feel.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When telling a suspenseful part of a story, a good storyteller often…
options: speaks faster and louder all the time
slows down and lowers their voice
questions.answer: slows down and lowers their voice
questions.hint: How do you build tension?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a pause most useful for in a spoken story?
options: Creating suspense or letting an idea sink in
questions.answer: Creating suspense or letting an idea sink in
questions.hint: Silence can be powerful.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What do we call the people listening to a performance?
questions.hint: They are watching and listening to you.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which opening would best grab an audience's attention?
options: Um, so this is my story.
On the darkest night of the year, a knock came at the door.
My story is about a boy.
I am going to tell a story now.
questions.answer: On the darkest night of the year, a knock came at the door.
questions.hint: Which one makes you want to hear more?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How might you change your voice for a character who is very old and tired?
questions.hint: Match the voice to the character.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is volume in spoken English?
options: How loud or quiet your voice is
questions.answer: How loud or quiet your voice is
questions.hint: You can turn it up or down.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which piece of feedback is most useful?
options: Your pause before the twist built suspense, but speak louder at the start.
questions.answer: Your pause before the twist built suspense, but speak louder at the start.
questions.hint: Useful feedback is specific and helps you improve.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When receiving feedback, a good response is to…
options: listen, thank the person and think about how to improve
questions.answer: listen, thank the person and think about how to improve
questions.hint: Feedback is a gift for next time.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which gesture would suit the line 'The giant stretched his enormous arms'?
questions.hint: Body language can show the meaning.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why do storytellers often repeat a key phrase during a story?
options: To make it memorable and build rhythm
Because they forgot the next line
questions.answer: To make it memorable and build rhythm
questions.hint: Think of traditional tales with repeated lines.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the best way to prepare for a storytelling performance?
options: Rehearse aloud several times, practising voice and pace
questions.answer: Rehearse aloud several times, practising voice and pace
questions.hint: Spoken skills improve by speaking.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Describe two ways you could use your voice to make the climax of a story exciting.
questions.hint: Think about pace, volume, pauses and intonation.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Give one piece of helpful feedback you could give a classmate after their storytelling, using 'What went well' and 'Even better if'.
questions.hint: Be kind and specific.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the main purpose of an advertisement?
options: To persuade people to buy or do something
To give instructions for a game
questions.answer: To persuade people to buy or do something

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What do we call a short, catchy phrase used to make a product memorable?
questions.hint: Think of a phrase you remember from a TV advert.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does the term 'target audience' mean?
options: The group of people an advert is aimed at
The company that pays for the advert
The actors in a TV advert
questions.answer: The group of people an advert is aimed at

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: An advert shows teenagers laughing together on skateboards while drinking a fizzy drink. Who is the most likely target audience?
questions.hint: Who would see themselves in the picture?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read the slogan: 'Fresh, fast and fantastic!' Which language technique does it mainly use?
questions.hint: Look at the first sound of each key word.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Tired of boring breakfasts?' Which persuasive technique is this?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Grab yours today!' What type of verb is 'Grab' here?
questions.hint: Is it telling the reader to do something?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: '9 out of 10 dentists recommend Sparkle toothpaste.' Which persuasive technique is used?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do many adverts use the pronoun 'you'?
options: To speak directly to the reader and make it feel personal
To show the advert is fiction
questions.answer: To speak directly to the reader and make it feel personal

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Hurry — offer ends Sunday!' What feeling is this line trying to create?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: An advert for a family car shows a sunny beach, smiling children and a dog in the back seat. What is the image mainly suggesting?
options: The car will bring happy family moments
The car is cheap to repair
The car is only for travelling to the beach
questions.answer: The car will bring happy family moments
questions.hint: Think about the feelings the picture creates, not just the objects.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which word in this slogan is most emotive? 'Give your pet the love it deserves.'

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which of these is a fact rather than an opinion in an advert?
questions.hint: Which one could be measured or checked?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: An advert for a toy is shown on TV between children's cartoons on a Saturday morning. What does the timing tell you?
options: The advertisers are targeting young children
The toy is only sold on Saturdays
questions.answer: The advertisers are targeting young children

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Explain how the colours and images in an advert can persuade the target audience. Use one example of your own.
questions.hint: Think about what bright, dark or natural colours make people feel.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why should readers think carefully about claims such as 'the best in the world' in adverts?
questions.hint: Can this kind of claim be proved?

fre.topic: The school day and il y a

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does 'il y a' mean in English?

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct article: Il y a ___ bibliothèque.
questions.hint: Bibliothèque is a feminine noun.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct article: Il y a ___ gymnase.
questions.hint: Gymnase is a masculine noun.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct article: Il y a ___ salles de classe.
questions.hint: The noun is plural.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into English: la cantine

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into English: la bibliothèque

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does 'le collège' mean for a French pupil aged 11–15?
questions.hint: False friend! It is not the same as the English 'college'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which sentence means 'There is a big playground'?
options: Il y a une grande cour.
Il y a des grande cour.
questions.answer: Il y a une grande cour.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: How do you say 'There isn't a swimming pool'?
options: Il n'y a pas de piscine.
Il y a pas une piscine.
questions.answer: Il n'y a pas de piscine.
questions.hint: After a negative, un/une/des usually becomes 'de'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French: there are

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which word is the odd one out (not a place in school)?

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct ending: Dans mon collège, il y a des ___.
questions.hint: 'des' needs a plural noun.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does this sentence mean? 'Il y a une cantine mais il n'y a pas de gymnase.'
options: There is a canteen but there isn't a gym.
There is a gym but there isn't a canteen.
There is a canteen and a gym.
There isn't a canteen or a gym.
questions.answer: There is a canteen but there isn't a gym.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French: a gym (use the correct article)

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which is the correct French sentence for 'In my school there is a library'?
options: Dans mon collège, il y a une bibliothèque.
Dans ma collège, il y a un bibliothèque.
Dans mon collège, il est une bibliothèque.
Dans mon collège, il y a des bibliothèque.
questions.answer: Dans mon collège, il y a une bibliothèque.
questions.hint: Check the gender of collège and bibliothèque.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write two sentences in French describing your school, using 'il y a' and 'il n'y a pas de'.
questions.hint: Example structure: Dans mon collège, il y a… mais il n'y a pas de…

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What makes a desert a desert?
questions.hint: Think about water, not heat.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Hot deserts usually receive less than how many millimetres of rain per year?
questions.hint: It is a number between 200 and 300.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which word means 'very dry, with little or no rain'?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which of these is the world's largest hot desert?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why are hot deserts often very cold at night?
options: There are few clouds to trap heat
The wind blows from the sea
questions.answer: There are few clouds to trap heat

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the name for a fertile area in a desert where water reaches the surface?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which adaptation helps a cactus store water?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why do cacti have spines instead of broad leaves?
options: To reduce water loss and protect from animals
questions.answer: To reduce water loss and protect from animals

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why do some desert plants have very long roots?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: How does a camel's hump help it survive in the desert?
options: It stores fat, which can be used for energy
It stores water like a tank
It helps the camel run faster
questions.answer: It stores fat, which can be used for energy
questions.hint: A common myth is that it holds water.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why are many desert animals nocturnal?
options: They can only see in the dark
There is more rain at night

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: How do the large ears of a fennec fox help it?
options: They let heat escape from its body
questions.answer: They let heat escape from its body

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Traditional desert clothing is often loose and covers most of the body. Why?
options: It protects from the sun and keeps air moving to stay cool
It is heavier and keeps people warm in the day
It makes it easier to carry water
questions.answer: It protects from the sun and keeps air moving to stay cool

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What word describes how plants, animals and people change to suit their environment?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain two ways that people living in hot deserts can adapt to the lack of water.
questions.hint: Think about where water comes from and how to save it.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Describe one challenge and one opportunity of hot deserts for people.
questions.hint: Think about the climate and about resources such as sunshine or minerals.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which English king conquered Wales in the late 13th century?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What word means taking control of a country or land by force?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Who was the Welsh prince killed in 1282 during Edward I's campaigns?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why did Edward I build huge stone castles in Wales, such as Caernarfon and Conwy?
options: To control the Welsh and show English power
To use as royal holiday homes
questions.answer: To control the Welsh and show English power

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Many of Edward's Welsh castles were built near the coast. Why was this useful?
options: They could be supplied by sea
The sea kept the stone dry
It was cheaper to buy land there
questions.answer: They could be supplied by sea
questions.hint: Think about what an army under attack would need.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What title did Edward I give his son in 1301, linking the English crown to Wales?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Edward I became involved in Scotland after Alexander III died. What problem did Scotland then face?
options: There was no clear heir to the throne
A plague that killed the king's army
questions.answer: There was no clear heir to the throne

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which Scottish leader won the Battle of Stirling Bridge in 1297?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year did Robert the Bruce defeat the English at the Battle of Bannockburn?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Who led the English army at the Battle of Bannockburn?
questions.hint: Edward I had died a few years earlier.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why was the Battle of Stirling Bridge a victory for the Scots?
options: The English were attacked while crossing a narrow bridge
questions.answer: The English were attacked while crossing a narrow bridge

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What nickname was Edward I given because of his campaigns against Scotland?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What happened to William Wallace in 1305?
options: He was captured and executed by the English
He signed a peace treaty with Edward I
questions.answer: He was captured and executed by the English

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which document of 1320 declared Scotland's independence and was sent to the Pope?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain why Edward I was more successful in conquering Wales than Scotland.
questions.hint: Think about castles, leaders and how the Scots resisted.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: How far do you agree that Robert the Bruce was more important than William Wallace in Scotland's fight for independence? Give a reason.
questions.hint: Compare what each leader achieved in the end.
